cards.title: Run Frontline Email Timing Test
cards.description: Before building anything, validate the end-to-end latency from when Frontline sends a job email to when a sub could realistically receive a push alert. This test de-risks the core value proposition.

checklist.text: Set up a test forwarding address (e.g. via Mailgun or SendGrid inbound parse webhook)
Have 2-3 real subs forward live Frontline job emails to the address
Log exact timestamps: Frontline send time, inbound receipt time, and simulated alert delivery time
Calculate median and worst-case latency across 20+ real emails
Document findings and set a latency SLA target (e.g. alert within 90 seconds of Frontline send)

cards.notes: Frontline emails may be batched or delayed on Frontline's side — if latency exceeds 3-5 minutes consistently, the product pitch needs to be reframed. Use this data in beta marketing copy. Mailgun inbound parse is free up to 100 messages/day for testing.

cards.title: Set Up Firebase Project and Auth
cards.description: Initialize the Firebase project with Authentication, Firestore, and Cloud Messaging enabled. This is the foundational infrastructure that all other services depend on.

checklist.text: Create Firebase project in console and enable Firestore in production mode
Enable Email/Password and Google OAuth providers in Firebase Auth
Enable Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) and save VAPID key
Set up Firebase environment config for dev and production environments
Create initial Firestore security rules restricting reads/writes to authenticated users

cards.notes: Store VAPID keys and service account credentials in Railway environment variables, never in source control. Set up a separate Firebase project for staging to avoid polluting production data during the parser dev phase.

cards.title: Build Frontline Email Parser on Railway
cards.description: Deploy a Node.js service on Railway that receives forwarded Frontline emails via inbound webhook, parses job details, and writes structured records to Firestore. This is the core data pipeline.

checklist.text: Scaffold Node/Express app and deploy to Railway with a health-check endpoint
Configure Mailgun or SendGrid inbound parse to POST to Railway webhook URL
Write regex/cheerio parser to extract: job date, school, district, grade, subject, pay rate, and job ID
Validate parser against at least 15 real Frontline email variants (different districts format differently)
Write parsed job object to Firestore jobs collection with sub's UID and received timestamp

cards.notes: Frontline email formatting varies significantly by NJ district — prioritize building a tolerant parser that logs unparsed fields rather than failing silently. Store the raw email HTML in Firestore alongside the parsed object so you can re-parse retroactively when the parser improves.

cards.title: Implement Push Alerts and SMS Backup
cards.description: After a job is parsed and matched to a sub's preferences, trigger a Firebase Cloud Messaging push notification and fall back to SMS via Twilio if the push is not acknowledged within 30 seconds.

checklist.text: Register FCM service worker in the React PWA and request notification permission on onboarding
Store FCM device tokens per user in Firestore and handle token refresh
Write Cloud Function or Railway endpoint that sends FCM push with job title, school, date, and one-tap Frontline deep link
Integrate Twilio SMS as fallback triggered after 30-second push non-acknowledgment
Log alert delivery status (sent, delivered, clicked) back to Firestore for the missed-job log feature

cards.notes: iOS Safari requires the user to add the PWA to their home screen before FCM push works — make this a prominent step in the onboarding flow. Twilio SMS costs roughly $0.0079/message; factor this into paid tier pricing. The one-tap link should deep-link directly to the Frontline job accept page using the parsed job ID.

cards.title: Build Preference Matching Engine
cards.description: Allow subs to set job preferences (districts, grade levels, subjects, minimum pay, days of week) and filter incoming parsed jobs so alerts are only sent for matching opportunities.

checklist.text: Design Firestore user preferences schema covering district whitelist, grade range, subject tags, min pay, and blackout dates
Build preference settings UI in React with multi-select controls for each dimension
Write matching function that compares parsed job object against stored preferences before triggering alert
Add a 'notify me anyway' override toggle so subs can temporarily receive all alerts
Test matching logic with edge cases: missing pay data, multi-grade jobs, district name variations

cards.notes: NJ district names in Frontline emails may not exactly match what subs expect to type — build a district name normalization map early. Consider letting subs import their Frontline district list during onboarding to reduce setup friction.

cards.title: Build Core PWA Shell and Onboarding Flow
cards.description: Scaffold the React/Vite PWA with a manifest, service worker, and a step-by-step onboarding flow that walks new subs through email forwarding setup, notification permission, and preference configuration.

checklist.text: Initialize React/Vite project with PWA plugin (vite-plugin-pwa) and configure manifest.json
Build onboarding stepper: create account, copy forwarding address, grant push permission, set preferences
Generate a unique inbound email address per user and display it clearly with copy-to-clipboard
Add 'add to home screen' prompt with visual instructions for iOS and Android
Implement protected routing so unauthenticated users always land on onboarding

cards.notes: The forwarding address setup step is the highest drop-off risk in onboarding — include a short GIF or screenshot showing exactly how to set up email forwarding in Gmail, Outlook, and Apple Mail. The unique per-user inbound address is how you tie inbound emails to a Firestore UID without requiring login on every forward.

cards.title: Implement Feed Health Check and 20-Day Tracker
cards.description: Surface a feed health indicator that warns subs if no emails have been received in 48 hours (likely a forwarding break), and track the 20-day substitute limit and credential expiration dates with proactive alerts.

checklist.text: Store lastEmailReceived timestamp per user in Firestore and run a daily Cloud Function to check for staleness
Send a push alert and in-app banner if no email received in 48 hours with troubleshooting steps
Build a credential tracker UI where subs enter their NJ substitute certificate expiration date
Send renewal reminder alerts at 60, 30, and 7 days before credential expiration
Build a 20-day counter that increments per accepted job and resets on a user-defined school year start date, with alert at day 18

cards.notes: The 20-day rule is specific to NJ subs without a teaching certificate — make the counter opt-in and clearly labeled so credentialed subs are not confused. The feed health check is a strong retention tool; a silent broken feed is the most common reason subs would churn.

cards.title: Build Missed-Job Log and Calendar Sync
cards.description: Give subs a searchable log of all jobs they were alerted to, whether they accepted or missed them, and allow them to sync accepted jobs to Google Calendar or iCal.

checklist.text: Display a paginated Firestore-backed job history list showing job details, alert timestamp, and accept status
Add a manual 'I took this job' toggle per log entry for subs who accepted directly in Frontline
Implement Google Calendar OAuth integration to push accepted jobs as calendar events
Generate an iCal feed URL per user as an alternative to Google Calendar OAuth
Add basic analytics summary: jobs alerted this month, jobs accepted, acceptance rate

cards.notes: Google Calendar OAuth requires verifying your app with Google if you request broad scopes — use the calendar.events scope only and consider iCal as the primary sync method to avoid OAuth review delays during beta. The missed-job log is a key sticky feature that creates a personal record subs will return to regularly.

cards.title: Launch Private Beta with 10-20 NJ Subs
cards.description: Recruit a small group of real NJ substitute teachers for a private beta, gather qualitative feedback, and validate that the full alert pipeline works reliably before opening to the public.

checklist.text: Recruit 10-20 beta testers from NJ sub Facebook groups, Reddit (r/njteachers), and local district sub lists
Create a simple beta landing page with waitlist signup and a short screener form
Set up a Slack or Discord channel for beta tester feedback and bug reports
Define success metrics: alert latency under 90s for 90% of jobs, zero missed alerts due to parser failure
Run a structured feedback session at day 7 and day 21 with all testers

cards.notes: Offer beta testers a free lifetime or heavily discounted tier as incentive — this also gives you a committed group for testimonials at public launch. Prioritize testers from multiple NJ districts to stress-test parser variation coverage early.

cards.title: Integrate Stripe and Launch Paid Tier
cards.description: Implement Stripe billing to gate premium features behind a monthly subscription, with a free tier that provides basic alerts and a paid tier that unlocks SMS backup, calendar sync, and the missed-job log.

checklist.text: Create Stripe products and price objects for free and paid monthly tiers
Integrate Stripe Checkout and Customer Portal using Firebase Extensions or a custom Railway endpoint
Store subscription status in Firestore and gate premium features in the React app using role-based checks
Set up Stripe webhooks to handle subscription created, updated, and canceled events
Add upgrade prompts at natural friction points in the free tier UI (e.g. when SMS backup would have fired)

cards.notes: Use Stripe's test mode extensively before going live — webhook handling for subscription lifecycle events has many edge cases. Consider a 14-day free trial of the paid tier for all new signups to reduce friction and increase conversion. Pricing suggestion based on comp: $7-9/month given the clear ROI for subs who accept even one additional job per month.
